text:
incident-bot: URGENT: Elevated 5xx + 429s observed across /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings from 18:40 UTC. Error rate spiking from ~0.5% to 8%. Auto-alerting on-call. Paging now. Incident ID: INC-2026-1800123456.

sanjay (oncall): seeing the alert. getting a quick take. any customer-facing impact metrics?

emily (support): multiple CS tickets flagged timeouts and some 429s for high-volume customers. One enterprise customer reported degraded realtime inference. No prod outage pages yet, but UX is degraded for burst traffic.

alex (infra): checking gateway logs — lots of 429s from our API gateway (kong-proxy) followed by backend 502/504 from runtime autoscale pressure. Logs show quota-manager returning 429s with header `X-Quota-Policy: global_quota_v2`.

jamie (eng-runtime): stack traces show connection flood to model workers. We might be hitting a misapplied quota config that forces global throttling, causing retries and cascading load. Searching recent config rollouts.

ops-bot: Deploy 1800123400 (quota-controller) finished at 18:38 UTC by alex. Rollout notes: global quota switch enabled for env=prod.

nate (sre): hypothesis: quota-controller enabled a strict global quota (units/sec) that doesn't account for per-customer bursts, gateway returns 429, clients retry, runtime overloads and returns 5xx. Need quick mitigation: relax global quota and enable per-tenant fallback.

sanjay (oncall): agree. what's the fastest safe action? rollback quota-controller? or patch config?

alex (infra): I can roll back the deployment to previous revision (1800123300) which had old behavior. Rolling now in canary -> will promote if stable. Command: `./deploy rollback quota-controller --rev 1800123300 --env prod --canary 10%`

ops-bot: Rollback started. Canary at 10%. Monitoring...

jamie (eng-runtime): while that's rolling back, recommend we also flip gateway to allow `x-retry-after` backoff by sending `Retry-After: 1` header to reduce client hammering. Patch in-flight via feature-flag `gateway-relax-retry` (hot patchable). I can flip it now.

nate (sre): flipping `gateway-relax-retry` true via config service. `curl -XPOST http://config-service/prod/flags -d '{"gateway-relax-retry":true}'` (applied)

alex (infra): canary rollback looks ok so far — 10% nodes healthy, 429 rate on those nodes down by ~60%. Promoting to 50%.

emily (support): notifying affected customers: sending targeted message to the flagged enterprise accounts: short note that we have transient throttling, mitigation underway. Maria on CS is coordinating.

maria (customer-success): messaging drafted. will send after we have confirmation that 50% rollback reduces errors. Trying to avoid alarm unless we can't stabilize.

jamie (eng-runtime): found the root: quota-template in repo `infra/configs/global_quota.yaml` was updated with unit mismatch — `requests_per_minute: 60000` intended to be per-cluster but was applied as per-node. That multiplied enforced limits by node count and triggered strict global enforcement. Opening diff: `-requests_per_minute: 60000
+requests_per_minute: 60000 # intended per-cluster, not per-node`

nate (sre): that explains cascade: gateway saw 429s -> client retries -> backend got thrashed -> 5xx. We'll revert the config and add a guard in deploy pipeline.

alex (infra): full rollback to previous config completed at 18:52 UTC. Monitoring metrics: 429 rate down from 6.8% to 0.9% over 5 minutes, 5xx down from 1.5% to 0.2%.

ops-bot: Canary and promotion logs: rollback promotion to 100% complete.

jamie (eng-runtime): follow-ups: 1) Add validation to quota-controller to detect per-node vs per-cluster units. 2) Add canary throttle on config changes (soft-limit for first 30m). 3) Add dashboard alert for 'quota-config-change' with human approval. I'll open tickets.

sanjay (oncall): customer impact assessment: EMILY — which customers saw errors and who needs an incident update?

emily (support): three enterprise customers reported user-facing errors (IDs in ticket: #CS-1023, #CS-1028, #CS-1031). One had timeouts for 8 minutes. We'll send an incident update: root cause, mitigation, and timeline + action items.

maria (customer-success): I'll coordinate postmortem comms and offer a credits package if they request.

nate (sre): runbook items executed: rollback quota-controller, flip gateway-relax-retry, increase runtime worker soft-cap for 10m to relieve backpressure (`kubectl scale deploy runtime-workers --replicas=60`), clear KV caches to avoid stale throttling tokens. Commands run and logs attached to incident ticket.

jamie (eng-runtime): added a temporary fallback route to send traffic to dedicated-pool for enterprise tenants to avoid global throttling while we complete validation. Route config: `route: /v1/* --> weight: dedicated-pool:80, default-pool:20` applied at 18:50 UTC.

alex (infra): infra note: the quota-controller rollout pipeline lacked schema validation on `requests_per_minute` units — adding CI lint and a preflight check now. PR #infra/789 opened.

ops-bot: Incident severity updated to sev2 at 18:54 UTC (widened customer impact).

sanjay (oncall): handing over to alex for the next shift at 19:00 UTC. I'll add handoff notes to the incident ticket: what we changed, rollback completed, metrics stable, action items pending.

alex (infra): taking over. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours and follow up on PRs for validation + add a temporary alert suppression window for config change alerts to avoid noise.

emily (support): sending an incident update email to affected customers now with ETA for postmortem.

maria (customer-success): capturing customer impact & compensation notes in the postmortem doc.

jamie (eng-runtime): final technical summary for postmortem: misapplied quota config (per-node vs per-cluster), caused global throttling -> retries -> backend overload -> 5xx. Mitigations: rollback, gateway retry relaxation, temporary routing to dedicated pool, runtime scale-up. Long-term fixes: schema validation, canary config throttles, per-tenant burst allowances.

nate (sre): monitoring dashboard shows stabilization. Will keep alert page open until green for 30m.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1800123456 transitioned to "Mitigated" at 19:08 UTC. Please add follow-up tasks and tag postmortem owners.

sanjay (oncall): thanks team — great coordination. I'll file the postmortem draft tomorrow and assign owners to the three action items. Marking handoff complete.

alex (infra): noted, will own infra validation ticket.

jamie (eng-runtime): will own runtime and routing follow-ups.

emily (support): will own customer comms + ticket updates.

maria (customer-success): will follow up with enterprise accounts.

nate (sre): closing monitoring runbook checklist now.

-- end of thread --
